agent_instructions.role: You are the senior full-stack engineer building this app together with the owner, who has limited coding experience. Explain what you are about to do in plain language before running commands or changing the data model.
agent_instructions.source_of_truth: This file defines the data model, business rules, features and acceptance criteria. PROJECT.md explains the why. CLAUDE.md holds coding rules and commands. If they disagree, this file wins for behaviour and CLAUDE.md wins for code style.
workflow: Work one feature at a time, in milestone order (M0, M1, M2, M3). Do not start a feature until every id in its depends_on list is done.
Before coding a feature: restate its acceptance criteria, list the files you will create or change, and point out anything in this spec that is unclear.
Ask the owner before any change to the data model, a new dependency, or anything listed in out_of_scope.

Write the tests for a feature's acceptance criteria first, then the code. A feature is done only when each criterion has a passing automated test or a written manual check, and `npm run check` passes.
Never guess a business rule. If the spec is silent or contradicts itself, stop and ask.
When a decision changes this spec, update spec.json in the same commit and add an entry to decision_log.
After finishing a feature, set its status to "done" in this file and summarise what changed in one short paragraph.
agent_instructions.kickoff_prompt: Read PROJECT.md, CLAUDE.md and spec.json in full. Then start milestone M0 (feature F-00): scaffold the project exactly as described in stack and repo_layout, create the D1 schema for every entity with Drizzle migrations, and deploy a page that says 'Hello' behind Cloudflare Access to the staging Worker. Explain each step in plain language before you run it, and stop for my confirmation before creating any Cloudflare resources.
agent_instructions.feature_prompt_template: Implement {feature_id} ({title}) from spec.json. First restate the acceptance criteria and list the files you will touch, then write failing tests, then the code, then run `npm run check`. Stop and ask if anything is unclear.

project.name: SME Invoice and Delivery Order App
project.summary: Internal web app for a small Malaysian business group to create branded quotations, invoices and delivery orders for several companies, and keep them as PDFs for 7 years.
project.users: 1 to 5 internal staff. No customer logins.
project.companies: Several legal entities, each with its own logo, registration number, address, bank details and document numbering.
project.language: English UI and documents for v1.
project.hosting: Cloud only (Cloudflare). Local machine is for development only.

business_context.myinvois_note: All companies, including related companies, are below RM3 million annual revenue, so MyInvois e-invoicing is not mandatory. Keep the optional fields listed under future_ready so it can be added later without a schema rewrite.
business_context.email_sending: Deferred to the next phase. v1 lets staff download PDFs and send them from their own mailbox.

sst: No company is SST-registered. Documents must not charge SST, must not show SST lines, and must be titled INVOICE, never TAX INVOICE.
Keep tax columns in the schema with default 0 and hide them in the UI while company.sst_registered is false, so registration later is a settings change.
record_keeping: Keep issued documents and their PDFs for at least 7 years.
Issued documents are never hard-deleted or edited. Corrections are made by voiding and re-issuing; a voided document keeps its number.
Every issued PDF is stored once in R2 with its SHA-256 hash recorded.
pdpa: Collect only what documents need: customer name, registration number, addresses, contact person, phone, email.
Do not store NRIC or passport numbers in v1.
Only staff who pass Cloudflare Access can reach any data.
Accept the data processing terms of Cloudflare and GitHub, and keep a one-page record of where data is stored (Cloudflare, APAC location hint).
Publish a short privacy notice to customers, in English and Bahasa Malaysia, saying invoices and contact details are kept in a cloud service.
A data protection officer is not required unless the business processes personal data of more than 20,000 people.

stack.runtime: Cloudflare Workers (one Worker serves the React app as static assets and the API under /api)
stack.validation: Zod, schemas shared between client and server in src/shared
stack.frontend: React + Vite + TypeScript, React Router, TanStack Query, Tailwind CSS, shadcn/ui
stack.database: Cloudflare D1 (SQLite), created with location hint "apac", read replication OFF
stack.orm: Drizzle ORM with drizzle-kit generated SQL migrations
stack.file_storage: Cloudflare R2: one private bucket for logos and issued PDFs, one private bucket for backups
stack.auth: Cloudflare Access (email one-time PIN) in front of the whole app; the Worker validates the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header on every /api request. v1 uses Worker-level Access on the workers.dev address, so no custom domain is needed
stack.pdf: Server-rendered HTML templates (Hono JSX) converted to PDF by Cloudflare Browser Run through the Workers browser binding (@cloudflare/puppeteer)
stack.testing: Vitest with @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers for API and service tests; Playwright for a few end-to-end flows
stack.ci_cd: GitHub Actions: check on every push, deploy to staging on main, deploy to production on a version tag
stack.backup: D1 Time Travel plus a nightly GitHub Actions job running `wrangler d1 export` into the backup R2 bucket
stack.versions: Use the latest stable version of each package at scaffold time and pin them in package-lock.json.

platform_limits.note: Workers Free plan limits that the design must respect. Checked 2026-11-24.
platform_limits.d1: Max database 500 MB; 5 million rows read and 100,000 rows written per day; 50 queries per Worker invocation (one db.batch counts as one); 100 bound parameters per query; 7-day Time Travel
platform_limits.r2: 10 GB storage free; no egress fees
design_consequences: Insert document lines with db.batch and chunk any multi-row insert so no statement has more than 100 bound parameters.
Keep CPU-heavy work (PDF rendering) in Browser Run, not in the Worker.
Generate a PDF once at issue time and serve the stored copy afterwards.

rules: One sequence per company and document type. It starts at 1000 and never resets, not monthly and not yearly.
The number has no year or month; the date lives in issue_date and seq_year is still recorded for reporting.
A number is assigned only when a draft is issued. Drafts have no number.
Numbers are gap-free: deleting a draft never uses up a number, and a voided document keeps its number.
seq grows past 9999 without breaking (it is padded to at least 4 digits).
Changing a prefix in settings affects only documents issued afterwards.
The number is a business convention, not a sales report: it starts high so low volume is not advertised. It stays consecutive and auditable.
numbering.implementation: D1 has no interactive transactions, so issue with one db.batch (which runs as a single transaction): (1) INSERT the sequence row if missing (INSERT OR IGNORE with next_value 1000); (2) UPDATE number_sequences SET next_value = next_value + 1 WHERE company_id = ? AND doc_type = ? AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM documents WHERE id = ? AND company_id = ? AND type = ? AND status = 'draft'); (3) UPDATE documents SET seq = (SELECT next_value - 1 FROM number_sequences WHERE company_id = ? AND doc_type = ?), seq_year = ?, number = (prefix || '-' || printf('%04d', seq)), status = 'issued', issued_at = ?, issued_by = ? WHERE id = ? AND status = 'draft'. Then verify the document now has a number; if not, return 409. Generate the PDF after the batch succeeds.

transitions.notes: Hard delete allowed only for drafts
Creates a draft invoice; allowed once unless that invoice is void

quotation.derived: Show 'Expired' in lists when status is issued and valid_until is before today. Expired is a label, not a stored state.
quotation.convert_rule: Converting an issued quotation first marks it accepted, then creates the draft invoice. There is no manual accept or reject step.

transitions.guard: Blocked while any non-void delivery order exists for this invoice

delivery_order.creation_rule: A delivery order can only be created from an issued invoice of the same company and customer.

calculations.total_sen: subtotal_sen - discount_sen + tax_sen; must be >= 0; tax_sen is 0 in v1
calculations.amount_in_words: English, upper case, e.g. 1250.50 -> 'RINGGIT MALAYSIA ONE THOUSAND TWO HUNDRED FIFTY AND SEN FIFTY ONLY'; 0 sen -> omit the SEN part
calculations.delivery_remaining: For each invoice line: invoice quantity_milli minus the sum of quantity_milli on lines of non-void delivery orders (draft, issued or delivered) that point to it

features.title: Project scaffold and deployment
acceptance_criteria: The repository matches repo_layout, and `npm run dev`, `npm run check`, `npm run deploy:staging` work.
Staging and production each have their own Worker, D1 database (location hint apac, read replication off) and R2 buckets.
Opening the staging URL without passing Cloudflare Access shows the Access login; after login a 'Hello' page shows the user's email.
Calling /api/me with an invalid or forged Access JWT returns 401, and a request with no Access session is stopped by Cloudflare Access before it reaches the Worker.
GitHub Actions runs `npm run check` on every push and deploys staging from main.

features.title: Users, roles and company membership
acceptance_criteria: A seeded owner can add a staff member by email to a company and set the role.
A user who passes Access but is not in users, or is inactive, gets 403 with a clear message.
Requests with an X-Company-Id the user is not a member of return 403 and no data.
Staff cannot call owner-only endpoints (403); tests cover every owner-only endpoint.

features.title: Company profiles, logo and switcher
acceptance_criteria: The owner can create several companies and edit every field in the companies entity.
Uploading a PNG or JPEG up to 1 MB stores it in R2 and shows it in settings and in the top bar; other files or larger files are rejected with a message.
Switching company changes every list and form to that company's data only.
SST, TIN and MSIC fields are hidden in the UI while sst_registered is 0.

features.title: Customers
acceptance_criteria: Staff can create, edit, search by name and archive customers of the current company.
Archived customers are hidden from pickers but still appear on existing documents.
Name and billing address are required; email is validated when present.

features.title: Items
acceptance_criteria: Staff can create, edit, search by name or SKU, and archive items.
SKU is unique within a company when set; a duplicate shows a field error.
Unit price accepts up to 2 decimal places and is stored in sen.

features.title: Document numbering service
acceptance_criteria: Issuing produces numbers in the numbering format, per company and type, starting at 1000.
Issuing 20 drafts in parallel for the same company and type yields 20 consecutive numbers with no duplicates or gaps.
Deleting a draft does not consume a number; a voided document keeps its number and the next issue gets the next value.
Numbers never reset: the first document of a new year continues from the previous number.
Issuing a document that is not a draft returns 409 and does not change any sequence.

features.title: PDF generation and archive
acceptance_criteria: Each document type renders to an A4 PDF matching pdf_layouts, with the company logo, and a 30-line document flows onto a second page with the table header repeated.
The HTML preview route and the PDF use the same template.
An issued document's PDF is generated once, stored in R2 under {company_id}/{type}/{year}/{number}.pdf, and served from R2 afterwards.
Draft PDFs show a DRAFT watermark and are never stored.
Voiding stores a separate VOID copy and keeps the original file unchanged.
If Browser Run fails, issuing still succeeds; the PDF is generated on the next download and the user sees a retry message, not an error page.

features.title: Quotations
acceptance_criteria: Staff can create a draft quotation by typing a customer name (an existing customer is reused on an exact name match, otherwise one is created with its billing address when the draft is saved) and by adding item-based or free-text lines, then edit and delete it.
valid_until defaults to issue_date plus the company's quotation_validity_days.
Totals follow calculations exactly; tests cover rounding with decimal quantities and line discounts.
Issuing freezes the customer and company snapshots, assigns a number, stores the PDF in R2 and records its SHA-256.
Issued quotations cannot be edited (409); the owner can void one with a reason. Acceptance is implied by converting it to an invoice (F-09).
Lists show an Expired label when issued and past valid_until.

features.title: Invoices
acceptance_criteria: Staff can create, edit and delete draft invoices with the same line editor as quotations.
due_date defaults to issue_date plus the customer's payment terms, else the company default.
Issuing freezes snapshots, assigns a number, sets amount_in_words and stores the PDF.
The PDF title is INVOICE and shows no SST, while the company is not SST-registered.
Only the owner can void, with a reason; voiding is blocked with a clear message while non-void delivery orders exist.

features.title: Convert quotation to invoice
acceptance_criteria: From an issued or accepted quotation, Convert creates a draft invoice with the same customer, lines, discounts, notes and reference, and source links on document and lines.
An issued quotation becomes accepted when converted.
A second conversion is blocked while a non-void invoice from that quotation exists.
The invoice view links back to the quotation, and the quotation view links to the invoice.

features.title: Delivery orders from invoices
acceptance_criteria: From an issued invoice, Create delivery order makes a draft with every line that still has remaining quantity, prefilled with that remaining quantity, and the customer's delivery address.
Staff can lower quantities or remove lines; a quantity above the remaining amount is rejected on save and on issue.
Several delivery orders per invoice are allowed (partial deliveries); the invoice view shows delivered and remaining quantity per line.
Delivery orders cannot be created from draft or void invoices.
No prices, discounts or totals appear in delivery order API responses, the DO editor or the DO PDF.
Mark delivered records delivered_at and the optional receiver name.
Voiding a delivery order returns its quantities to the invoice's remaining amount.

features.title: Lists, search and dashboard
acceptance_criteria: Each document list filters by status, customer and date range, and searches by number or customer name.
Lists page at 50 rows and load in under 1 second with 5,000 documents in staging.
The dashboard shows drafts, the 10 latest issued documents and invoices with undelivered quantities.

features.title: Audit log
acceptance_criteria: Issue, void, accept, reject, convert, mark delivered, company setting changes and member changes write an audit_log row in the same batch as the change.
The owner can view the audit log for the current company, newest first.

features.title: Backups and restore drill
acceptance_criteria: A nightly GitHub Actions job exports the production D1 database with `wrangler d1 export` and stores it, compressed, in the backup R2 bucket under backups/YYYY/MM/DD.sql.gz.
An R2 lifecycle rule keeps backups for 7 years.
A documented restore drill rebuilds staging from last night's export, and the drill has been run once before go-live.
RESTORE.md explains, in plain language, both D1 Time Travel restore and restore from an export.

features.title: CSV export
acceptance_criteria: The owner can export documents of a type and date range as CSV with number, date, customer, status and total in RM.
The file opens correctly in Excel with Malaysian dates and two-decimal amounts.

decision_log.why: Near-zero cost, no servers to manage, owner's preference

decision_log.decision: Use Cloudflare D1 instead of Neon Postgres
decision_log.why: Companies are not SST-registered and below the MyInvois threshold, PDPA impact is light, and one vendor is simpler for an AI-assisted build. Drizzle keeps a move to Postgres possible

decision_log.decision: v1 scope is quotations, invoices and delivery orders
decision_log.why: These are the documents used every day; payments, expenses, email and MyInvois come later

decision_log.decision: Delivery orders are created from issued invoices, with partial deliveries
No SST and no foreign currency in v1
decision_log.why: No company is SST-registered and all invoicing is in MYR

decision_log.decision: Use Worker-level Cloudflare Access on the workers.dev address instead of a custom domain
decision_log.why: Workers-level Access protects the workers.dev hostname, routes and previews, so v1 needs no domain. The owner keeps the .my domain for a later move without changing the app

decision_log.decision: Document numbers are PREFIX-1042: no year, sequence starts at 1000 and never resets
decision_log.why: The owner does not issue much volume and did not want numbers that advertise that. A high starting offset achieves it while staying consecutive and gap-free for accounting; random numbers were rejected because they would break gap-free numbering, ordering and explainability
The owner does not use customer PO numbers; the field was removed from the data model, the API, the PDFs and the editor

decision_log.decision: Quotations have no manual accept or reject step
decision_log.why: Nothing gates on acceptance, and converting to an invoice already implies it. Statuses are draft, issued, void, with accepted set only by conversion

decision_log.decision: Items live under Settings, not in the bottom bar
decision_log.why: The catalogue is set up rarely; the bar stays short: Home, Quotes, Settings, with Invoices added in F-08

decision_log.decision: A document can be created from a typed customer name instead of picking one
decision_log.why: Staff know the buyer's name before they have a customer record. The name is matched case-insensitively, reused when it matches exactly, and otherwise a customer is created when the draft is first saved
